answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF: many dependent modular squarings whose next input is unavailable until the prior result is known. GPUs cannot parallelize one chain to eliminate its sequential delay; however, separate clone identities can run separate chains in parallel, at added hardware and energy cost. Thus a gale of clones is constrained by per-identity proof time and aggregate resources, not prevented by a universal single-chain bottleneck. Challenges labeled jade or sonnet follow the same rule.
